generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

(a) Table of values

Step 1: substitute each value of \(x\). For each \(x\), first work out the angle inside the brackets, \([[if test="is(un=1)"]]x [[if test="is(cdeg>0)"]]-[[else]]+[[/if]] {@abs(cdeg)@}^\circ[[else]]x [[if test="is(cdeg>0)"]]-[[else]]+[[/if]] {@abs(crad)@}[[/if]]\), then find its [[if test="is(fs=1)"]]sine[[else]]cosine[[/if]]. For example, at [[if test="is(un=1)"]]\(x = 120^\circ\): \(y = [[if test="is(fs=1)"]]\sin[[else]]\cos[[/if]]\left({@inner5d@}^\circ\right) = {@dispdp(yv[5],2)@}\)[[else]]\(x = \frac{2\pi}{3}\): \(y = [[if test="is(fs=1)"]]\sin[[else]]\cos[[/if]]\left({@inner5r@}\right) = {@dispdp(yv[5],2)@}\)[[/if]].

The completed table, with the missing values shaded, is:

\(x\)\([[if test="is(un=1)"]]0^\circ[[else]]0[[/if]]\)\([[if test="is(un=1)"]]30^\circ[[else]]\frac{\pi}{6}[[/if]]\)\([[if test="is(un=1)"]]60^\circ[[else]]\frac{\pi}{3}[[/if]]\)\([[if test="is(un=1)"]]90^\circ[[else]]\frac{\pi}{2}[[/if]]\)\([[if test="is(un=1)"]]120^\circ[[else]]\frac{2\pi}{3}[[/if]]\)\([[if test="is(un=1)"]]150^\circ[[else]]\frac{5\pi}{6}[[/if]]\)\([[if test="is(un=1)"]]180^\circ[[else]]\pi[[/if]]\)\([[if test="is(un=1)"]]210^\circ[[else]]\frac{7\pi}{6}[[/if]]\)\([[if test="is(un=1)"]]240^\circ[[else]]\frac{4\pi}{3}[[/if]]\)\([[if test="is(un=1)"]]270^\circ[[else]]\frac{3\pi}{2}[[/if]]\)\([[if test="is(un=1)"]]300^\circ[[else]]\frac{5\pi}{3}[[/if]]\)\([[if test="is(un=1)"]]330^\circ[[else]]\frac{11\pi}{6}[[/if]]\)\([[if test="is(un=1)"]]360^\circ[[else]]2\pi[[/if]]\)

(b) Drawing the graph

(c) Describing the shift

Step 3: compare with \(y = [[if test="is(fs=1)"]]\sin[[else]]\cos[[/if]] x\). The new graph has exactly the same shape: the amplitude is still \(1\) and the period is still [[if test="is(un=1)"]]\(360^\circ\)[[else]]\(2\pi\)[[/if]]. Every point has moved sideways by the same amount.

[[if test="is(cdeg>0)"]]Subtracting inside the brackets, \(x - [[if test="is(un=1)"]]{@amt@}^\circ[[else]]{@amt@}[[/if]]\), moves the graph to the right. The peaks now happen \([[if test="is(un=1)"]]{@amt@}^\circ[[else]]{@amt@}[[/if]]\) later.[[else]]Adding inside the brackets, \(x + [[if test="is(un=1)"]]{@amt@}^\circ[[else]]{@amt@}[[/if]]\), moves the graph to the left. The peaks now happen \([[if test="is(un=1)"]]{@amt@}^\circ[[else]]{@amt@}[[/if]]\) earlier.[[/if]]

Final answer: the graph of \(y = [[if test="is(fs=1)"]]\sin[[else]]\cos[[/if]] x\) moves [[if test="is(cdeg>0)"]]to the right[[else]]to the left[[/if]] by [[if test="is(un=1)"]]\({@amt@}^\circ\)[[else]]\({@amt@}\) radians[[/if]].

Remember: \(y = [[if test="is(fs=1)"]]\sin[[else]]\cos[[/if]](x - c)\) moves the graph \(c\) to the right; \(y = [[if test="is(fs=1)"]]\sin[[else]]\cos[[/if]](x + c)\) moves it \(c\) to the left.
